cards.back: conduct research / conduct a study / conduct an experiment. Example: 'The team conducted extensive research into the effects of urbanization.'
draw conclusions / draw comparisons / draw attention. Example: 'It is difficult to draw definitive conclusions from such a small sample size.'
reach a consensus / reach an agreement / reach a compromise. Example: 'After lengthy negotiations, the committee reached a consensus on the new policy.'
raise awareness / raise concerns / raise questions. Example: 'The campaign was designed to raise awareness about the dangers of plastic pollution.'
pose a threat / pose a risk / pose a challenge. Example: 'Antibiotic resistance poses a serious threat to global public health.'
address an issue / address a problem / address a concern. Example: 'Governments must address the issue of income inequality before it worsens.'
significant impact / profound impact / detrimental impact. Example: 'Social media has had a significant impact on the way young people communicate.'
profound effect / adverse effect / lasting effect. Example: 'Childhood experiences can have a profound effect on adult behavior.'
growing concern / growing trend / growing demand. Example: 'Air pollution in major cities is a growing concern among health professionals.'
widely accepted / widely recognized / widely regarded. Example: 'It is widely accepted that education is the key to economic development.'
highly controversial / highly effective / highly unlikely. Example: 'The use of animal testing remains highly controversial among scientists and ethicists.'
increasingly important / increasingly difficult / increasingly common. Example: 'Digital literacy is becoming increasingly important in the modern workplace.'
gain insight / gain experience / gain access. Example: 'Through this study, researchers gained valuable insight into consumer decision-making.'
exert influence / exert pressure / exert control. Example: 'Multinational corporations can exert considerable influence over government policy.'
bear resemblance / bear responsibility / bear in mind. Example: 'The current economic situation bears little resemblance to the crisis of 2008.'
play a vital role / play a crucial role / play a pivotal role. Example: 'Education plays a vital role in reducing poverty in developing nations.'
take into account / take into consideration. Example: 'Policymakers must take into account the long-term environmental consequences of their decisions.'
shed light on / shed new light on. Example: 'Recent archaeological discoveries have shed light on the daily lives of ancient civilizations.'
stark contrast / sharp contrast / marked contrast. Example: 'The wealth of the capital stands in stark contrast to the poverty of rural areas.'
vested interest / vested authority. Example: 'Oil companies have a vested interest in slowing the transition to renewable energy.'
foregone conclusion. Example: 'Given the overwhelming evidence, the outcome of the trial was a foregone conclusion.'
empirical evidence / compelling evidence / anecdotal evidence. Example: 'There is strong empirical evidence linking regular exercise to improved mental health.'
underlying cause / underlying reason / underlying principle. Example: 'Poverty is often the underlying cause of many social problems in urban areas.'
inherent flaw / inherent risk / inherent limitation. Example: 'There is an inherent flaw in any system that relies solely on self-reported data.'
make a distinction / make a contribution / make a case. Example: 'It is important to make a distinction between correlation and causation in research.'
give rise to problems / give rise to debate / give rise to concerns. Example: 'Rapid technological change has given rise to new ethical dilemmas in the workplace.'
come to fruition / come to terms with / come to light. Example: 'After years of planning, the government's infrastructure project finally came to fruition.'
overwhelming majority / overwhelming evidence / overwhelming support. Example: 'The overwhelming majority of scientists agree that human activity is driving climate change.'
pivotal moment / defining moment / watershed moment. Example: 'The invention of the internet was a pivotal moment in the history of communication.'
paradigm shift. A fundamental change in approach or underlying assumptions. Example: 'The rise of artificial intelligence represents a paradigm shift in how businesses operate.'
